xtmux-fll.description:
PROBLEM
The operator requirement is to see dispatched specialists as ACTIVE and with their STATUS, nested under the dispatcher. The lineage half now exists (unitAI-vc7tl: @agent_parent_session / @agent_parent_pane stamped on specialist panes, verified end to end 2026-09-13). The status half does not: a specialist pane carries no @agent_state at all, so the picker renders a role badge derived from the session name and no lifecycle state.

The executor that landed the lineage half flagged this explicitly and stopped on it: "follow_ups: [@agent_state writer needs xtmux value contract before implementation]". That is the correct call - @agent_state is xtmux's vocabulary, written today only through scripts/agent-state.sh, and a second writer invented on the specialists side would fork the semantics.

This is a decision bead: settle the contract, then the writer becomes a small implementation item in the specialists repo.

PROPOSED CONTRACT (decide, amend, or reject)
- Single writer: the specialist runtime MUST write through ~/.tmux/scripts/agent-state.sh, never by setting the option itself. That keeps @agent_last_transition, @agent_instance_id and the off-path metadata clearing in one place.
- Vocabulary: reuse the existing set unchanged - running | needs-input | done | idle | off. No new states for specialists.
- Mapping: at launch (pane created, job about to run) -> running; while the job waits for operator input -> needs-input; when the job completes and the session stays alive (keep-alive) -> done; on session teardown -> off. idle is the pre-launch/post-instance state if a distinct one is wanted.
- Instance identity: the launch must use --new-instance so a reused pane cannot wear the previous job's instance id (the same rule the pi extension follows).
- Not-in-tmux: a headless run writes nothing; absence of state is the documented "no pane, nothing to visualize" case.
- Nested dispatch: the child's state is written on the child's own pane; the parent's state is not touched.
- The specialists runtime must not write @agent_parent_* (that is the lineage contract, already landed) and must not write @agent_bead/@agent_task/@agent_role unless xtmux already defines the source env for them.

SUCCESS
- The contract is decided and recorded, including the mapping table and the off/teardown behaviour.
- A specialist dispatched from a tmux pane shows a state badge in the picker within one poll of launch, and its @agent_last_transition advances.
- The dispatcher requirement is then fully satisfiable: nested row + role + live state.

SCOPE
- This bead: the decision and its record only.
- The writer itself: a follow-up item in the specialists repo (the runtime side), cross-referenced here.

NON_GOALS
- Progress, percent, ETA, or any richer telemetry: the operator asked for active + status, nothing more.
- Changing the existing state vocabulary or agent-state.sh semantics.
- The display nesting work, which is xtmux-oj2.

CONSTRAINTS
- One writer, one vocabulary: any divergence forks the semantics the picker, the topology projection and the attention ranking all read.
- The writer must be best-effort and bounded: a launch must not fail or stall because a tmux option could not be written.
- Do not clobber metadata written by other paths (a specialist pane may also carry @agent_bead from its launch contract).

VALIDATION
- After the writer lands: dispatch a specialist from a tmux pane and assert @agent_state advances running -> done (and off on teardown) with @agent_last_transition advancing, in an isolated tmux server.
- Assert the picker shows the state badge on the nested row.

OUTPUT
The decided contract recorded here; then a dispatchable specialists-side item for the writer.
